## DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE

The root cause of the test failure was in the `outerHtmlHead()` method of the `DocumentType` class. When generating the HTML/XML representation of a DOCTYPE declaration, the code handled the case where both PUBLIC_ID and SYSTEM_ID are present, and the case where only PUBLIC_ID is present. However, it failed to properly handle the case where only SYSTEM_ID is present (without PUBLIC_ID).

The bug was at line 61 of the original code: when a SYSTEM_ID existed without a PUBLIC_ID, the code would output just `" \"<systemId>\""` instead of `" SYSTEM \"<systemId>\""`. This caused DOCTYPE declarations like `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM "exampledtdfile.dtd">` to lose the SYSTEM keyword and become invalid.

The fix adds a check: when appending a SYSTEM_ID, if there is no PUBLIC_ID present, we must first append the literal string `" SYSTEM"` before appending the quoted system ID value.
